recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-18394; any future issue with current registry wording or navigation should be handled in the FHIR-extensions workflow.
issue_request: FHIR-18394 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core clarification asking that the old extensibility registry page define its scope by changing the generic Extension Registry label to FHIR Core-defined Extension Registry and clarifying that the listed extensions were defined in the FHIR specification.
initial_application: The requested scope wording was applied in commit db9355a66d9e549d3043a73c6aef8c9f6e40b46b, which changed source/extensibility-registry.html to use FHIR Core-defined Extension Registry for the title/header and to say the listed extensions were defined in the specification with the http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ base URI. The Jira comment from Grahame Grieve says the work was already done.
additional_context: Commit 4118eb9ddb6eabe52c56c903b3932f27c2c42e38 later deleted source/extensibility-registry.html and removed extension registry/version-map pages from active publish.ini entries because the content moved to the extensions IG. Current core publish.ini keeps extensibility.html, extensibility-definitions.html, and extensibility-examples.html active while extensibility-registry.html is commented out. The FHIR Extension Pack checkout now owns extension-registry.md, whose opening text already scopes the registry list as extensions defined in that specification with the same base URI. Later FHIR-extensions issues FHIR-43634 and FHIR-47833 confirm registry page behavior is an Extension Pack concern, not a reason to edit FHIR-core for this old issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The original core page was historically corrected and is no longer in the current core build, so editing core source now would be out of scope or redundant.

related_jiras.note: Published FHIR-extensions decision about Extension Pack registry navigation; confirms the current registry is managed as part of the Extension Pack with deliberate core integration.
